title: Advanced Analytics
tagline: PIVOT, LATERAL, advanced frames, sampling — analytics beyond GROUP BY

placementQuiz.q: PIVOT rotates rows to columns. In PostgreSQL, PIVOT is:
options: Done via crosstab() from tablefunc extension
placementQuiz.explain: PostgreSQL uses crosstab() from tablefunc extension for pivot. MySQL has PIVOT syntax in 8.0+.

placementQuiz.q: LATERAL join allows the right side to:
placementQuiz.explain: LATERAL allows right subquery to reference columns from left side of join.

placementQuiz.q: Advanced frame: ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING includes:
options: 2 rows before, current, 2 rows after (5 rows total)
placementQuiz.explain: 2 PRECEDING + current + 2 FOLLOWING = 5 rows total centered on current.
TABLESAMPLE SYSTEM samples at page level. Returns approximate percentage.

placementQuiz.q: LATERAL with LIMIT 1 for top-N per group — execution:
options: Index seek + LIMIT per outer row
placementQuiz.explain: LATERAL + ORDER BY + LIMIT with index on (partition, order) = index seek + LIMIT per outer row.

blocks.md: Static PIVOT works when categories are known. Dynamic PIVOT generates columns at runtime. Multi-level PIVOT (e.g., year → quarter → month) requires chaining or dynamic SQL. PostgreSQL: dynamic crosstab via execute format().

blocks.label: dynamic crosstab
blocks.pg: -- Dynamic SQL with EXECUTE format() for unknown columns
blocks.mysql: -- MySQL: prepared statements with dynamic SQL
blocks.py-pandas:
# Dynamic pivot
df.pivot_table(index='dept', columns='quarter', values='sales', aggfunc='sum')

blocks.label: multi-level pivot
blocks.code:
-- Static multi-level: year → quarter
SELECT * FROM crosstab(
  'SELECT year, quarter, SUM(sales) FROM sales GROUP BY year, quarter ORDER BY 1,2',
  'SELECT DISTINCT quarter FROM sales ORDER BY 1'
) AS ct(year INT, q1 NUMERIC, q2 NUMERIC, q3 NUMERIC, q4 NUMERIC);

-- True multi-level requires dynamic SQL or application-level pivot
-- Dynamic: build column list at runtime
blocks.pg: -- Chain crosstab calls or use dynamic SQL
blocks.mysql: -- MySQL: multiple PIVOTs or dynamic SQL
blocks.py-pandas:
# Multi-level pivot
df.pivot_table(index='year', columns=['quarter', 'month'], values='sales', aggfunc='sum')

blocks.md: Static crosstab requires known columns. For dynamic categories, use EXECUTE format() with dynamic SQL. Performance: dynamic SQL prevents plan caching.

items.explain: EXECUTE format() builds query string at runtime. Column list built dynamically.

options: Chain crosstab calls or build composite key
items.explain: Chain crosstab calls or build composite key (year||'-'||quarter) then pivot.

blocks.label: lateral top-n per group
blocks.code:
-- Top 3 products per category by sales
SELECT c.name, p.name, p.sales
FROM categories c
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT name, sales
  FROM products p
  WHERE p.category_id = c.id
  ORDER BY p.sales DESC
  LIMIT 3
) p ON true;

-- With ROW_NUMBER alternative (no LATERAL)
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT p.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category_id ORDER BY sales DESC) AS rn
  FROM products
)
SELECT * FROM ranked WHERE rn <= 3;
blocks.pg: -- LATERAL is often clearer for top-N per group
blocks.mysql:
-- MySQL 8.0.14+: LATERAL supported
-- ROW_NUMBER() alternative works everywhere

blocks.md: LATERAL + LIMIT is often faster than ROW_NUMBER() for Top-N: stops scanning after N rows per group. ROW_NUMBER scans all rows then filters.

blocks.label: lateral + aggregate
blocks.code:
-- For each customer: total orders, avg order value, latest order date
SELECT c.name,
  COALESCE(oa.total_orders, 0) AS total_orders,
  oa.avg_order,
  oa.latest_order
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT 
    COUNT(*) AS total_orders,
    AVG(total) AS avg_order,
    MAX(order_date) AS latest_order
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.customer_id = c.id
) oa ON true;
blocks.py-pandas:
# GroupBy agg
orders.groupby('customer_id').agg(
    total_orders=('id', 'count'),
    avg_order=('total', 'mean'),
    latest_order=('order_date', 'max')
).reset_index()

items.q: LATERAL vs ROW_NUMBER() for Top-N: which is faster when N is small?
items.explain: LATERAL + LIMIT stops after N rows per group. ROW_NUMBER scans all rows first.

options: Columns from LEFT side of join
items.explain: LATERAL allows right side to see left side columns. Like correlated subquery in FROM.

blocks.label: groups frame
blocks.code:
-- GROUPS: counts groups of peer rows (same ORDER BY value)
-- 1 group = all rows with same ORDER BY value
SELECT 
  salary,
  COUNT(*) OVER (
    ORDER BY salary
    GROUPS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING
  ) AS peer_count
FROM employees;

-- Useful for: percentile buckets with variable row density

blocks.md: SYSTEM sampling is fast but can be skewed if data clustered on pages. BERNOULLI is statistically sound but scans all rows. REPEATABLE(seed) for reproducible samples.

options: Peer groups (rows with same ORDER BY value)
items.explain: GROUPS counts peer groups (rows with same ORDER BY value). Useful for percentile buckets with ties.

items.q: TABLESAMPLE SYSTEM vs BERNOULLI — SYSTEM is:
items.explain: SYSTEM samples pages (fast, ~1% I/O). BERNOULLI samples rows (accurate %, full scan).

revisionCard: Dynamic PIVOT: EXECUTE format() builds column list at runtime
LATERAL + LIMIT 1/3 = efficient Top-N per group; stops after N rows per group
GROUPS frame (PG14): counts peer groups (ties); great for percentile buckets
TABLESAMPLE SYSTEM = fast page-level; BERNOULLI = accurate row-level
Dynamic SQL with EXECUTE format() for runtime column generation
LATERAL + aggregate = multiple aggregates per row in single lateral subquery

glossary.def: PIVOT where category columns determined at runtime via dynamic SQL.
Frame unit = peer groups (rows with same ORDER BY value). PostgreSQL 14+.
Page-level sampling. Fast (~1% I/O) but may be skewed if data clustered on pages.
Row-level sampling. Statistically accurate but scans all rows.
TABLESAMPLE option for deterministic sampling using seed.
SQL constructed at runtime (e.g., EXECUTE format() in PostgreSQL).
